utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I interrupted --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- can be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- it will be tendered and you can give your explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P00364, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You can give your explanation now, please.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to say that he got in touch with me and asked me about this but we never discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to have the next document 65 ter 565 being shown to this witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is, while it comes up, another press article in the same magazine we just discussed from 1st of May, 2001, almost two years later. And I'm interested in the B/C/S and both versions in page 3. And in English it is the second-last paragraph and in B/C/S it's the left column and the ninth line from the bottom there. We only need the left column here. You could probably scroll down a bit for the witness, the ninth line from the bottom. Scroll down, please, you are scrolling up. Fully down, please. Thank you. I think that's it, yeah. I'm reading to make it a little bit easier, if you could read it silently just for the record. The paragraph starts with: "Sperlic, chief of Kladovo OUP ..." What I'm interested in is a sentence which comes a little bit lower. "In order to suppress rumours, it was agreed to spread the word that the bodies were of the Kurds who tried to cross the border into Romania." Does that information tell anything to you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, what you read out. I see that again this is a newspaper article. I don't have full insight into everything, but what you just read out regarding the Kurds, yes, that is quite correct and that is what was done, we agreed. The chief, Sperlic, and me, and some other people in the local police agreed to spread the rumour that the Kurds were escaping the war and the bombing in Serbia because there was an incident a couple of days prior to this about 50 kilometres upstream some person - now, whether they were Kurds or not - they had crossed the state border without documents. And so this gave us the idea because a large number of people had seen not the whole thing but partially what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To whom was this information provided in order to suppress the rumours?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: To no one in particular. Kladovo is a small town. We all know each other there. I was a policeman, as were the others, and we knew whom we should tell and we knew -- telling him to keep quiet about it, but we knew that he would pass it on immediately. So we knew the people that we should give such information to and they would spread it further, people sitting around in cafes, in restaurants. This is normal for the police, to know such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So do you know that indeed these people sitting around in cafes were approached with that rumour -- regarding that rumour?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I went to talk one or two of them, who asked me what had happened and I said, just some Kurds wanted to escape and the truck skidded into the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And looking back now, was it successfully suppressed, the rumours, by providing that story and for long if so?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: People stopped talking about it soon, and when the government changed in Serbia all this came out into the open. So if you want an explanation, I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just -- can you maybe give me a year and, if you can, even a month in which the government changed and everything came to light?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When it changed, the year 2000 I think. And this is already -- it was already in 2001 that everything came out into the open. And I'll explain, if you wish, how this is done. The Timocka Krimi review is a local paper appearing in the region of Zajecar and there are the neighbouring municipalities, Bor, Majdanpek, Negotin. And this Timocka crime review published it today, but it is not published in Belgrade nor is it sold there in Belgrade, Novi Sad, or Nis but only within the region. And when this Timocka Krimi Revija published the news in the morning already the next morning all the newspapers in Serbia published it on the front page. So it's hard to explain how quickly this reached Belgrade, but all this was prepared in advance, and the word was that it should be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I seek to tender this document 65 ter number was 565, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00365, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to come back to the bodies inside the truck. Could you first of all tell me whether there were also female bodies found in the truck itself?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Roughly how many female bodies, or, if you don't know, how many percentage you now think were females?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I saw all the bodies and had contact with them, I don't think that there were more than ten or so female bodies, about ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And from your evidence I also gathered that there were two children in addition to the females, yeah?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a boy and a girl were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what clothes looking at the more than 80 bodies, what clothes did these -- all these persons wear?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: They all had civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you notice any uniforms, a single uniform among them?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, there wasn't a single uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter number 568 shown to this witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And while it comes up, we see and I also mentioned in the summary, this is from a press conference here held on the 25th of May, 2001. My first question is: Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we scroll it up, please, so the witness can see the heading also. And the English could be enlarged a little bit if it's possible because I don't think it's easy to read for Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I have. I saw it five minutes after it was completed due to various circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you first of all tell me -- it says here UKP and I'm talking about the second line of the header here?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It is the administration of the criminal police of the MUP in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who in 2001 headed the UKP?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The head was General Knezevic. Yes, I'm quite sure, General Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And to who did Mr. Knezevic report to in 2001 if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: To the minister, probably the minister. I'm not too familiar with the organisational structure in the MUP, but probably the minister as head of the crime police -- no, I apologise, I made a mistake, to the head of the department for public security. It is to him that he reported. He was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know in 2001 who the head of the department of public security was?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was General Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here - and please look at the last paragraph in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We need to scroll it down for the witness and in the English it's the fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- that your name is also mentioned in this. And I'm just referring to the last sentence here which says -- and this is referring to the bodies found in the truck: "Several male bodies wore UCK uniforms." What would your comment be --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, that's a mistake in writing this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, did you tell to anybody from the MUP in Serbia that information which is depicted here that any of the bodies were wearing UCK uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did provide that information, but not in the refrigerator truck, in another place. When they wrote this information, they mixed the two cases up. And due to the circumstances, when this information was being drafted, it had already been prepared. I was in Belgrade at the time and I told the author of this information that this was a mistake, and then he called up General Lukic and told him that the last sentence was wrong and he corrected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So -- but your evidence today is that you made it clear in relation to the refrigerator truck bodies and the bodies found there, there were no UCK uniforms found on the bodies and that's what you always stated? I'm just trying to summarise correctly.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so. I -- that is what I said in my statement, as did the other colleagues who were involved with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation could I seek to tender 65 ter 568 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00366, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Moving on to the next document 573 is the next 65 ter number. If we could enlarge it for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, this is mentioning -- this document is mentioning your name a couple of times. My first question would be: Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. This is the basic document and the first one made in connection with this case. I saw it during the trial of Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Milutinovic and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And does this document accurately reflect what you had stated to the working group established under the MUP roof in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, I agree with this official note, but I would like to point out that this is not my statement. This is a different form of a report. The official note was prepared by the working group on the basis of a -- an interview with me, and then this interview was conveyed in this note and there is some deviation. But in principle that is what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, Witness, is it correct that you have not signed this official note?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I don't sign such an official note. If it had been a statement then I would have had to sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we go to page 5 in English, and I need the third paragraph, please, and in B/C/S I would need page 6. Thank you. And in B/C/S it's the second paragraph from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all -- yeah, I give you a little time to read this. It starts with: "Bosko has information" here for Your Honours' benefit.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, could you tell Your Honours who is Bosko?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I am Bosko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That's your nickname, yeah?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. And is this relating here to the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: If I may be allowed, I would like to explain the second part of this official note.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would first ask you one or two questions, and then you are given the chance to explain. The question is: Does this photograph relate to the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. It appears as if I'm taking up time, but I don't see in this paragraph any mention of the refrigerator truck, and my learned friend is asking him to comment on the refrigerator truck. So in this paragraph there's no reference to the refrigerator truck -- oh, yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this the paragraph commencing: "Bosko has information ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it is, I see two references to the refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Near the end of the paragraph, Mr. Djurdjic. Carry on, please, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What -- I can be more precise. Is this referring to the refrigerator truck before it fell into the Danube?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this refers to that but only on the basis of certain information. It is not evidence. It is the stories that were going around afterwards because I checked this out a couple of days after the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Who provided that information which is stated in this paragraph to you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Rade Bogdanovic told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who is Mr. Bogdanovic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: He's currently retired. He worked in a company. He was a director in Termovent, but I wish to underline that these were not verified information. They were given to the working group to check them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you inform me whether Mr. Bogdanovic had personally observed the information which is stated in the paragraph here?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Probably he did, otherwise he wouldn't have told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. There's mentioning made here of two jeeps and people in camouflage uniforms. Could you verify from Mr. Bogdanovic whether the -- to which force or to which unit, if any, these jeeps and the people in the camouflage uniform belonged to?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. They passed in a car. It was night-time. He saw those two jeeps for a moment. It was in the night. It was late at night. I can't tell you exactly what the time was or what he said to me when this was, but he just saw that. I don't know whether this has any connection to the refrigerator truck or not, but he said -- he told me what he had seen that night on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then there is mentioning made that -- and I think that's a few paragraphs below -- two paragraphs below: "Bosko stresses everything fits chronologically. The refrigerator truck went through Gornji Milanovac, where it was seen. After the tunnel the jeeps were seen without the refrigerator truck, and then the same people and jeeps were seen at the GP." What is "GP" standing for?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me say first of all that is the difference between an official note and a statement. Here in the note, the author says Gornji Milanovac which is about 300 kilometres from Donji Milanovac. It should say here Donji Milanovac. That's a mistake. And GP stands for border crossing, the Djerdap border crossing toward Romania. So this is not Gornji Milanovac but it should be Donji Milanovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Djerdap - I may pronounce it wrongly -border crossing, how far away from Tekija is it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: About 12 kilometres, 12, 13 kilometres downstream towards Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document with a 65 ter number 573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00367, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you now to Petrovo Selo, and this is transcript page 7453 in the Milutinovic case, Your Honours, where you mention to have blown up the truck. First you said it was incinerated and then blown up by you in Petrovo Selo. Sir, tell me at what location --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- did this occur in Petrovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: This occurred -- I think it was on the 7th, that is, it was set alight; and on the 8th it was blown up at a facility which used to be a military facility a shooting range, then later it belonged to the Territorial Defence, afterwards to the police. So it was a training-ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, sir, in 1999 who operated that facility where you blew the truck up?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who was in charge. For a while it was under the SUP of Zajecar, then in 1999 it was under the MUP of Serbia, the MUP of Serbia was running this polygon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want now to ask you a little bit about the exhumations - and I'm switching to a separate event here, the exhumations. Could you tell me in late May 2001 what happened?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In late May 2001 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have a reference that's in the summary to these 2001 exhumations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe this is what -- relating to the objection my learned friend has made at the very beginning. I personally have not written the summary, and I have to say as far as I understand, there is no explicit reference to Petrovo Selo in the summary as such. But I also believe that it is explicitly stated in the witness's statement, and he even gives during his statement an explanation about the KLA uniforms and where the comment about the KLA uniforms is coming from. So he clarifies issues coming out of the refrigerator incident, and I think I'm giving this witness now also a chance to explain further what he meant with this remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying this is referred to in this report or this --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, this is referred to, first of all, in page 3 of the witness's statement. It is referred also in the document which I have tendered a moment ago, the 2001 report from the Ministry of Interior. I walked the witness particular to this passage relating to the KLA uniforms, and I thought I'm giving the witness a further possibility to explain what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm looking at the Serbian version, and this is page 3, the Tribunal's investigator is showing this 26th of June Serbia MUP information, it's about 2001 of course, stating that some male bodies wore KLA uniforms, and then the witness answered that none of the bodies in the refrigerator truck had KLA uniforms on them. Therefore, there is no reference at all to any exhumation in this statement. To go back to something that I've noticed several times already, there is the substance of the witness statement that is reflected in the summary, but it is not consistent with reality. I will from now on always react appropriately as soon as I have realised that the substance of the statement is not accurately and faithfully reflected in the summary provided. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can clear this up I hope very quickly. This is also from page 3 of the statement which I tendered I think it was the first exhibit today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exhibit P358.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. It says: "I agree with all this except the comment about the KLA uniforms. This has been confused with the exhumations carried out at Petrovo Selo where I was the Crime Technician." And this is indeed the sentence upon which I am trying to elaborate. It is explicitly stated there that there were exhumations, that the witness was a crime technician. I believe it is all clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue to clarify what is being dealt with in that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you first of all tell me whether, as you stated, you were a crime technician there, in Petrovo Selo in May 2001.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who requested your services to attend as a crime technician the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: If I may, I'm facing a problem here talking about this case. I made a statement about the refrigerator truck incident in the Milosevic trial and in the Milutinovic trial. What I see written here what is being challenged the KLA uniforms that were not there was already quite familiar back in 2006. No one asked me a question about it. Back in 2001, if I may be given a chance to explain this, back in 2001 I was told that I would be making a statement about the refrigerator truck incident. I may as well address this now because I have been shown a number of documents by the Prosecutor. Nevertheless, I only found out two days ago that I would be expected to address this subject too, which I can, but I was a technician so I like to keep things precise. I'm not best prepared to deal with this right now, but I think it should be up to you to decide whether I will embark on this or not. I did do that. I was involved in that exhumation with the Nis Institute back in 2001; that much is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the interpretation is correct, I heard that the witness was only shown this two days ago, what he's supposing to be addressing now and what he is being examined on now by my learned friend and that is precisely what I said a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, for clarification, this witness has talked in the Milutinovic case, and that's page 7455, also about the exhumations of the mass grave at Petrovo Selo, and that's lines 11 and 12. It's not the first time -- I mean, I'm prepared just to lead just a few facts from this witness, which he has observed as a crime technician and not to go into the details of the issue, if Your Honours permit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I find that there seems to be two issues, one you are dealing with, one Mr. Djurdjic is dealing with. And I'm not sure of the factual foundation for what Mr. Djurdjic is saying. Is it that the only exhumations that you will be referring to with this witness arise from this reference to excavations at Petrovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours. I want the witness to clarify this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the only context in which they are mentioned is to explain what the witness says is a mistake in reference to KLA uniforms in connection with the bodies in the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if possible confusion thereof which went into a document which was officially distributed, as the witness has explained to Your Honour a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, what are you concerned about with that, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness says that he set the record straight back in June 2006 and now he quotes the official note that was published. He said -- he drew the attention of the person who compiled the note to this and that this was conveyed to General Lukic. He told us that this very afternoon. Therefore, any reference to any exhumation, if we look at all of the witness's statements, in 1999 no reference at all to an exhumation. I think that is clear if we look at the statements, and the witness confirmed this for our benefit some minutes ago. It wasn't before two days ago that the witness actually talked to the Prosecutor about the exhumation, and that is another thing that the witness has clearly shared with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment, Mr. Djurdjic, I am not able to grasp the difficulty you are dealing with. There is in this document, which is on our screen, a reference in the communique to there being several male corpses in KLA uniforms in the refrigerated truck. The witness is -- it is his evidence, right or wrong is another matter, but it is the witness's evidence that that was not the case, there were no bodies in the refrigerated truck in KLA uniforms, that he expects that the reference to KLA uniforms results from a confusion because he did see KLA uniforms among bodies which were exhumed at Petrovo Selo. Nothing to do with the refrigerated truck at all. So the only reference to this exhumation is to say it was another lot of bodies, another incident, and they got confused. Now, is that a problem for you? Otherwise, thank you. Carry on, please, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm trying to finish now. I would have finished a long time ago, and I hope that the objection time doesn't count for my examination time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, I tried to keep it clear before, we don't keep a stopwatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We look at the approximate time as a guide, and we hope people can keep to it. Untoward events happening, we take notice of and allow the time to be extended without any question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, this is anyway my last line of questioning here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Will it finish in two minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because if it won't, Mr. Neuner, it's better that you do it in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... morning, then I try to be finished within a few minutes and I promise Your Honours to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, because I can see that you have reached the point where you probably have too much to conclude satisfactorily tonight. Now, I believe tomorrow we are sitting in the afternoon. I wrongly assumed morning, which means everyone can make mistakes when they say things. And that, therefore, means we must adjourn now. We resume tomorrow at 2.15, and we must ask you if you would return tomorrow to continue with your evidence and the Court staff will assist you with arrangements overnight and tomorrow. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of March, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
